reason: Meets archival, canonical-path, concurrency, crash and one-time requirements with no authorization/plan/query/transport schema changes. One local utility alone is insufficient: narrow runner authorization gates and package/source authority update are necessary. Versioned paths additionally touch transport reread identity without removing these requirements.

exactModifyPaths.responsibility: Capture-only integration: acquire shared lifecycle lock before reading canonical authorization; verify READY receipt and fresh explicit approval; persist one-time consume claim before CaptureTransport construction/credential access; retain lock through rollback, durable capture receipt and consumed archival/outcome. No new runner CLI flag, query, target, transaction or backup change.

Add capture_authorization.py to package_hashes; advance sole CAPTURE_APPROVAL reference from historical v4 to future v5. Keep /2 field set, validators, risk binding, DRAFT/READY gates and 900-second rules unchanged. No v4 fallback.

Lifecycle unit, multiprocess concurrency, owned filesystem crash injection, privacy and runner-before-credential tests; adapt capture runner harness to required lifecycle records and forward authority assertions, retaining existing IDs/business assertions.

Owned runner integration proves consume-before-connect, one session/read-only/rollback, durable baseline/outcome and no replay after success/failure. Move regression outputs off finalized directories to new exclusive per-run directory before running any regression subprocess; preserve historical expectations and fixtures.
Document official local mint interface, fresh approval trust boundary, rotation/consumption/crash states, recovery STOP rules, immutable archives, v5 prerequisite and forward test outputs.

exactAddPaths.responsibility: One formal local-only lifecycle utility plus runner context API: fixed plan paths, strict external single-capture approval validation, per-plan flock, durable approval/nonce claims, archival non-replacing rename, staged /2 mint, final READY receipt, consume claim, terminal archival/outcome. No DB/network/credential reads, transport imports or runner dispatch.

exactScope.scopeExpansionStop: Any implementation path beyond these six, any fixture/product/migration/query/DB schema change, or new package/image dependency requires STOP and separate scope approval.

concurrencyMechanism.selected: persistent per-plan fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) + O_EXCL durable claims
concurrencyMechanism.lockLifetime: Mint holds lock for all validation/archive/stage/publication; runner holds same lock from canonical read until rollback, receipt write, consumed archival and outcome finalization.
concurrencyMechanism.lockFile: 0600 owner-only regular nlink1 O_NOFOLLOW O_CLOEXEC; created exclusively when absent, otherwise validated; never unlink/recreate lock inode. Validate fd identity against directory entry before action.
concurrencyMechanism.failure: LOCK_BUSY stops immediately; no waiting loop, PID timeout takeover or automatic retry.
concurrencyMechanism.flockLimitation: Advisory cooperating-process serialization, not defense against root or an operator editing files outside protocol. Trusted OS-operator boundary retained.
concurrencyMechanism.durableClaims: ApprovalId, explicit USER approvalReferenceSha256 and new nonceSha256 each get separate permanent O_EXCL claims before publication; source proposal raw SHA is NOT used as the per-attempt approval reference. Every partial/malformed existing claim burns that identity and blocks reuse. The auth raw SHA consume claim is durable before credentials.
concurrencyMechanism.O_EXCLOnlyAlternative: Can serialize but stale crash lock requires a new recovery protocol; use flock for live lock and durable phase state for crash stop.
concurrencyMechanism.privateDirectoryOnlyAlternative: 0700 protects ownership but does not serialize two same-UID operators.
concurrencyMechanism.FDInheritance: Lock fd close-on-exec; inherited DB children must not prolong lock. Parent crash still leaves consume/incomplete phase records denying replay/new mint.

compare.A_LEAVE_UNTIL_EXPIRY: Unsafe by itself: current capture nonce is syntax-only and authorization could be reused within900s.
compare.B_ARCHIVE_ONLY_AFTER_CAPTURE: Unsafe by itself: concurrent/crashed capture can reuse before archive.
compare.C_DURABLE_CONSUME_THEN_ARCHIVE: Chosen: durable pre-dispatch claim rejects replay regardless of finalizer/crash.

runnerGuardOrder: Read canonical safely; authorize_capture validates current /2
Require exact-hash READY and phase continuity, both fresh user-approval claims plus nonce reservation bound to that READY, no unresolved prior operation, stage open and all bound authorities
Check canonical hash not consumed; exclusive fsync consumed claim before constructing CaptureTransport
Call existing CaptureTransport.capture with same canonical bytes; keep canonical stable for runtime guard rereads
Existing READ ONLY/REPEATABLE READ/query order/ROLLBACK unchanged
After transport close, exact-hash rename canonical into archive; write exclusive outcome binding baseline receipt raw SHA or safe failure code
Release flock; print SUCCESS only when baseline receipt and lifecycle outcome both durable; failures never restore authorization
oneTimeConsumptionMechanism.nonClaims: Consume record proves authority reserved, not that DB connected. Capture receipt proves persisted baseline; outcome links them without changing readonly-baseline-capture/2 public schema.
oneTimeConsumptionMechanism.finalizerFailure: Consumed claim remains authoritative; no retry or reactivation, root result BLOCKED_LIFECYCLE_FINALIZATION even if capture receipt exists.
oneTimeConsumptionMechanism.reuseExistingHelpers: Reuse safe_file, strict_json, canonical, sanitized, Failure and exclusive patterns. Do not instantiate Engine or reuse migration Journal vocabulary as a capture apply attempt. receipts.py remains unchanged.
oneTimeConsumptionMechanism.internalAPIBoundary: Supported production authority path is formal runner CLI; lifecycle is not an OS sandbox against root or a trusted operator invoking internal Python APIs outside the approved process.

archivePolicy.collision: FAIL even identical bytes; no overwrite/dedup
archivePolicy.reason: Forward lifecycle preservation, not legacy cleanup
archivePolicy.canonicalAfterCompletion: Absent after consumed archival; if crash/IO failure leaves it present, durable consumed record makes it inactive. Expired files may physically remain until approved rotation, but are never active.
archivePolicy.firstArchiveProvenance: SHA/inode exact rename of existing legacy raw file; known use comes from first-capture attempt and proof hashes. No fictional historical consume receipt is invented: a NEW bootstrap historical-used reservation records this provenance.

crashSafety.durableState: Old bytes still canonical; may have PREPARED/claims only.
crashSafety.failClosed: Old authorization expired or lacks lifecycle READY; runner rejects. Any incomplete operation blocks next mint. No automatic approval/nonce reuse.

crashSafety.durableState: Old preserved in archive; canonical absent.
crashSafety.failClosed: Runner rejects missing canonical. No old fallback, move-back or automatic mint. Incomplete phase requires separate forward recovery decision.

crashSafety.durableState: Pending0600 file and STAGED record may exist; canonical absent.
crashSafety.failClosed: Runner never scans pending/archive; no dispatch. Retain orphan pending bytes as evidence; do not publish on restart.

crashSafety.durableState: New auth may occupy canonical but final rotation READY absent/partial.
crashSafety.failClosed: Runner requires valid exact-hash READY under same lock before credentials; reject. Even an unexpired schema-valid canonical file is insufficient.

crashSafety.durableState: Exactly one complete published auth and final valid READY exist.
crashSafety.failClosed: Mint is committed; no duplicate mint or replay. Only a later separately invoked runner may consume that one fresh approval. Utility never dispatches.

crashSafety.durableState: Consumed claim exists, even if malformed; DB may never have been opened.
crashSafety.failClosed: Authorization burned, second runner denied. No claim deletion/retry; state described as local dispatch claimed, not DB activity proven.

crashSafety.durableState: Consumed claim durable, canonical may remain; baseline may or may not be durable.
crashSafety.failClosed: Same authorization cannot replay; unresolved outcome prevents new lifecycle mint. Preserve UNKNOWN/NOT_PERSISTED as appropriate; no recovery of memory or control-flow-only success.

futureOperatorApprovalContract.kind: Future trusted operator attestation of a NEW explicit user approval; utility validates but NEVER creates/invents the approval.
futureOperatorApprovalContract.approvalId: fresh32hex; O_EXCL claim, never reused even after aborted mint
futureOperatorApprovalContract.referenceRule: New safe immutable approval-attestation reference/path + exact SHA; cannot reuse the first or blocked second capture user approval. Local user-attestation bytes are not cryptographic proof of conversation authenticity.
futureOperatorApprovalContract.freshness: Finite numeric times, no bool, not future, unexpired, maximum window900s; authorization expiry cannot exceed this explicit approval expiry.
futureOperatorApprovalContract.credentialIdentitySource: Read only previously approved non-secret identity evidence or exact legacy authorization to extract its identity digest with provenance. Reconstruct target from fixed profile, never copy old authorization as new template. Actual credential bytes only checked by future formal runner. If no independently bound digest exists, STOP; do not read credentials to manufacture it.
futureOperatorApprovalContract.noOldApprovalReuse: Old per-attempt approval reference/ID is historical only. /2 userApprovalRef remains the fixed SOURCE proposal reference; unique fresh USER approval is separately bound by READY+consume receipts. These two concepts must not be conflated.
futureOperatorApprovalContract.absentFileCase: Only explicit expectedCanonicalState=ABSENT and no unfinished lifecycle records permits initial mint.
futureOperatorApprovalContract.referenceUniqueness: Reserve both approvalId and approvalReferenceSha256 in separate immutable claim namespaces; changing ID cannot reuse the same user approval evidence. Cryptographic binding is to the attestation bytes, not a claim of automatic chat authenticity verification.
futureOperatorApprovalContract.credentialProvenancePathPolicy: The evidence path is only a checked reference to a source-proposal-authorized safe evidence artifact or the exact current/archived old authorization; never an arbitrary readable path and never connectionDirectory. Reject any provenance outside that finite allowlist.

futureSourceAuthority.captureReceiptContract: readonly-baseline-capture/2 UNCHANGED; new lifecycle outcome binds its exact raw SHA externally
futureSourceAuthority.whyRunnerMustChange: Mint-only utility cannot stop direct formal runner replay before expiry or dispatch from canonical after crash-before-READY; current capture never creates Journal/claim. Gate must run before CaptureTransport constructor because constructor reads credentials.
futureSourceAuthority.currentV4: UNCHANGED_HISTORICAL_SOURCE_AUTHORITY; no future mint under changed source
futureSourceAuthority.v5Generation: Only after implementation+owned validation+fresh package hashes; proposal approved=false executionAuthorized=false; no v5 generated in A1. Future production mint/capture needs new explicit user approval, not current implementation proposal or blocked second approval.
futureSourceAuthority.v4ReferenceReconciliation: Literal v4 execution binding cannot survive source/package changes. Preserve exact v4 SHA as historical authority chain; /2 userApprovalRef forwards only to v5. Unique per-capture user approval is separately enforced via lifecycle receipts without inventing /2 fields.
